title: World 1: The Python Realm
tagline: Begin your coding quest and master the core foundations
description: Welcome to the enchanted kingdom of PyQuest! Awaken your magical coding potential as you learn Python syntax, manipulate elemental variables, and conjure interactive spells.

levels.title: The Spark of Syntax
levels.description: Learn what Python is, master statement syntax, and cast your very first print() invocation.

lessons.title: Welcome to Python
lessons.content: Python is a versatile, beginner-friendly programming language celebrated for its clear and readable syntax. In PyQuest, Python code acts like magical incantations—giving instructions directly to your computer.
lessons.codeExample:
# A simple incantation
print('Greetings, Python Adventurer!')
lessons.tip: Python instructions execute from top to bottom, one statement after another.

lessons.title: The print() Spell
lessons.content: The `print()` function is one of the most essential spells in your repertoire. It displays messages, data, and computation results to the console output screen.
lessons.tip: Text strings inside print() must be wrapped in matching quotation marks, like 'single' or "double" quotes.

challenges.title: Syntax Trial
challenges.instructions: Test your grasp of Python syntax by selecting the valid command to display a message on screen.
challenges.question: Which of the following correctly outputs 'Hello Adventurer' in Python?
hints: Think of the built-in function we just learned with parentheses.
challenges.explanation: In Python, print() is the built-in function used to output text or numbers to the console.

challenges.title: The First Incantation
challenges.instructions: Cast your first spell! Write a Python program that prints the exact message: 'Hello Python' to the console output.
challenges.starterCode: # Write your code below to print Hello Python
hints: Wrap Hello Python in quotation marks inside the parentheses.
challenges.explanation: Awesome work! print('Hello Python') calls the print function with the string 'Hello Python', transmitting it to the screen.

levels.title: The Alchemy of Variables
levels.description: Harness data containers: craft strings, store integers, measure floats, and balance booleans.

lessons.title: Variables: The Magic Jars
lessons.content: A variable is like a labeled jar that stores data for later use. In Python, you create a variable simply by naming it and using the `=` assignment operator.
lessons.tip: Variable names in Python should use lowercase letters and underscores (snake_case).

lessons.title: Core Elemental Data Types
lessons.content:
Python has four foundational primitive types:
• **str (String)**: Text like 'Dragon' or "Excalibur"
• **int (Integer)**: Whole numbers like 10, -3, 100
• **float (Float)**: Decimal numbers like 99.5, 3.14
• **bool (Boolean)**: True or False
lessons.codeExample:
quest_title = 'The Dragon Quest'
health_points = 100
critical_chance = 0.25
is_alive = True
lessons.tip: Booleans in Python are capitalized: True and False.

challenges.title: Identifying Data Elements
challenges.instructions: Inspect the value 42.0 and determine its data type in Python.
challenges.question: What is the data type of 42.0 in Python?
hints: Notice the decimal point .0 attached to the number.
Numbers with decimal fractions are floating-point numbers.
challenges.explanation: Because 42.0 contains a decimal point, Python treats it as a float rather than an integer.

challenges.title: Assigning Hero Stats
challenges.instructions: Create a variable named `mana` and set it to `100`. Then, print the value of `mana`.
challenges.starterCode: # Create mana variable and print it
hints: On the next line, call print(mana) without quotation marks.
challenges.explanation: Great job! Printing a variable name without quotes outputs the value stored within that variable.

levels.title: The Scroll of Interaction
levels.description: Communicate with users using input(), perform type conversions, and evaluate arithmetic expressions.

lessons.title: Gathering Input from Players
lessons.content: The `input()` function pauses execution and waits for the user to type something. Whatever the user types is always returned as a **string** (`str`).
lessons.codeExample:
# Reading user text
user_name = input()
print('Welcome, ' + user_name)
lessons.tip: Because input() always yields a string, you must convert it if you want to perform math!

lessons.title: Type Conversion & Math Powers
lessons.content:
Convert strings to numbers with `int()` or `float()`. Python also provides elemental operators:
• `+` Addition, `-` Subtraction
• `*` Multiplication, `/` Division
• `**` Exponentiation (Power), `%` Modulo (Remainder)
lessons.codeExample:
base_attack = int('20')
buff = 5
total_attack = base_attack + buff
print(total_attack)
lessons.tip: Use int(input()) when you need to read whole numbers from the user.

challenges.title: Predict the Alchemy
challenges.instructions: Analyze the Python snippet below and predict what will be printed.
challenges.question:
What is the output of the following code?
x = '3'
y = '4'
print(x + y)
hints: Both '3' and '4' are strings wrapped in quotes.
The + operator concatenates (joins) two strings together.
challenges.explanation: When the + operator is used between two strings, Python concatenates them, producing '34'. To get 7, you would convert them to integers with int().

challenges.title: The Power Calculation
challenges.instructions: Write a script that reads an integer number from the user using `input()`, calculates its square (multiplied by itself), and prints the result.
challenges.starterCode: # Read integer from input, calculate square, and print it
hints: Convert input() to an integer: n = int(input())
Compute the square: n * n (or n ** 2)
challenges.explanation: Brilliant! You successfully converted standard input into an integer and calculated its square across test cases!
